extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, research integrity officers, and interested scientific readers
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluative standards and expectations for journal editors when handling allegations of research misconduct and deciding whether to retract, flag, or otherwise address published papers. Includes considerations of timeliness, deference to institutional investigations, transparency, and adherence to community guidelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editors' collective responsibility for the integrity of the published record
rubrics_metrics.description: "Editors of medical journals have a collective responsibility for the integrity of the published record. When notified of ethical breaches they have an imperative to act, and when faced with a formal decision on scientific misconduct they should ensure that the paper be retracted or removed."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a formal decision on misconduct exists, editors should act to retract or remove the paper; failure to respond undermines trust in medical publishing and research. Example: Karolinska expects Respiration to retract a paper found to involve misconduct.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeliness — avoid undue delay in responding to allegations
rubrics_metrics.description: Journals are often criticized for taking too long to act on allegations about research — or failing to do so altogether. Sometimes that’s because they’re waiting for institutions to complete their investigations. But that’s not the case here, as Ottersen notes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editors should not indefinitely delay action when an institution has completed its investigation and reached conclusions; prompt responses are required when patient safety or clinical practice may be affected.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag unresolved concerns with an expression of concern
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case at hand the reader will not even find an expression of concern.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If editors decide not to retract immediately, they should at minimum flag the paper with an expression of concern so readers are aware there are unresolved integrity issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency and providing a forum for debate
rubrics_metrics.description: The journal argued it was 'not in a position to make a judgement on whether or not to retract this article' and therefore proposed publishing KI’s argument for why the paper should be retracted, along with a rebuttal from the authors. 'We believe... we are not in a position to make a judgement... We do not want to patronize the readers.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One editorial approach is to publish the arguments and rebuttals transparently and allow readers to form their own opinions, rather than making a definitive retraction decision when editors believe the evidence is insufficient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deference to independent institutional investigations
rubrics_metrics.description: Some commenters argued 'Journals should fully respect the decision of an independent investigation.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an independent and credible institutional investigation reaches findings of misconduct, journals should give serious weight to those findings and consider acting (retraction/flagging) accordingly rather than treating the matter as open-ended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adherence to community standards (ICMJE/ICJME recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respiration requested ICMJE include the journal on their list of those accepting ICMJE recommendations. ICMJE recommendations on Scientific Misconduct, Expressions of Concern, and Retraction are cited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journals should follow established community guidelines (ICMJE et al.) on handling misconduct, expressions of concern, and retractions and should not claim adherence if they do not follow those standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data access and independent verification
rubrics_metrics.description: A commenter asked whether independent researchers can have access to the original data of the published research at issue and argued: 'If not, the paper should be summarily rejected as prima facie bogus.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing anonymized/raw data for independent verification is an important safeguard; lack of data access may justify skepticism, critical scrutiny, or retraction if claims cannot be independently validated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jurisdiction and authority: journals make the final retraction decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Anonymous commenter: 'Whether to retract is simply not KI’s decision. They can (and should) advise the editors as to what evidence they’ve uncovered, and the editors should take this into account, but KI is not in charge of the process or the final decision.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions should present their evidence and recommendations, but editors/publishers retain the final authority to decide on retraction; constructive engagement between institutions and journals is advised rather than coercive tactics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of public disclosure/pressure as a tactic
rubrics_metrics.description: Ottersen posted parts of his correspondence with the journal to put pressure on the journal editor to do the right thing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions or complainants may publicly share correspondence to pressure editors; this is a pragmatic tactic but raises concerns about confidentiality, fairness, and process — editors should consider whether public pressure affects impartial decision-making.
